bulletins.title: Microsoft Outage Tech Support Impersonation
bulletins.summary: Scammers are exploiting recent Microsoft outages by contacting consumers and businesses offering fake assistance. Posing as IT help desks, banks, or police, they attempt to gain remote access, steal account credentials, or extract payments under the guise of restoring services.

bulletins.title: Grandparent and Family Emergency Phone Scams
bulletins.summary: Callers pose as panicked grandchildren or relatives claiming to be in an urgent crisis, such as an arrest or car accident. They plead for immediate bail or emergency funds while pressuring the victim to keep the call secret from other family members.

bulletins.title: VA Disability and Benefits Fast-Tracking Fraud
bulletins.summary: Fraudsters contact military veterans via phone, SMS, and direct message impersonating Department of Veterans Affairs personnel. They demand upfront fees with deceptive promises to guarantee a 100 percent disability rating or fast-track pending benefit claims.

bulletins.title: Federal Trade Commission Agency Impersonators
bulletins.summary: Imposters pose as Federal Trade Commission agents using fraudulent phone calls, messages, and spoofed websites. They convince targets that their identity has been compromised or that funds can be recovered if they transfer funds or disclose financial details.

gemini_context_snippet: Active phone scams this week feature urgent family emergency calls claiming a grandchild needs bail, alongside service outage tech support impersonation and fraudulent VA representatives demanding upfront fees to increase disability ratings.
